value: magnetic compass orientation disrupted by a weak broadband electromagnetic field; not disrupted by the relatively strong narrow-band fields employed
units: orientation (Rayleigh test of group mean vector)
eye: whole animal (light-dependent radical-pair mechanism proposed; receptor not tested)
method: Emlen funnels (35 cm diameter, 15 cm high, 45 degree walls) in an electromagnetically silent purpose-built laboratory; orientation scored from scratches; group mean vectors tested with the Rayleigh test, conditions compared with the Mardia-Watson-Wheeler test
conditions: wild robins caught on the University of Oldenburg campus, housed indoors; 91 birds over spring 2012 (32), spring 2013 (21), autumn 2013 (17) and spring 2014 (21); only birds pre-tested as oriented in the natural (NMF) and changed field (CMF, magnetic north turned 120 degrees counterclockwise, ~48,600 nT) entered the critical tests; field settings and scoring blinded; no randomised sequence of conditions is described; autumn 2013, same 16 birds per condition: broadband (~2 kHz to ~9 MHz per the abstract) NMF 265 degrees, r = 0.17, p = 0.63; CMF 21 degrees, r = 0.19, p = 0.57 (Results text; Figure 6 caption prints p = 0.603 and 0.557); dummy NMF 313 degrees, r = 0.54, p < 0.01, CMF 96 degrees, r = 0.49, p < 0.05; 1.315 MHz (~48 nT peak, 71 nT summed) NMF 281 degrees, r = 0.56, p < 0.01, CMF 20 degrees, r = 0.62, p < 0.001; no MWW comparison of broadband against dummy or 1.315 MHz is reported (disorientation rests on non-significant Rayleigh tests); broadband summed intensity 35 nT (10 kHz to 10 MHz) calculated from a measured spectrum, below the 71 nT of the autumn narrow-band field; spring 2012 ~48 nT narrow-band: 1.363 MHz r = 0.25, p = 0.138, N = 31; 2.726 MHz r = 0.24, p = 0.179, N = 30; dummy 17 degrees, r = 0.43, p < 0.01, N = 31; MWW among the three p = 0.771; spring 2013 ~400 nT: 50 Hz p < 0.05 (N = 19), 1.363 and 2.726 MHz p < 0.01 (N = 20 each), MWW p = 0.415; spring 2014 1.315 MHz ~48 nT: oriented in NMF (r = 0.64, p < 0.001, N = 18) and CMF (r = 0.42, p < 0.05, N = 20), dummies oriented (N = 16 and 18)

source.authors: Schwarze S, Schneider N-L, Reichl T, Dreyer D, Lefeldt N, Engels S, Baker N, Hore PJ, Mouritsen H
source.title: Weak Broadband Electromagnetic Fields are More Disruptive to Magnetic Compass Orientation in a Night-Migratory Songbird (Erithacus rubecula) than Strong Narrow-Band Fields

where: Abstract (sentence read in pieces on the frontiersin.org full-text page and the publisher PDF)
quote: Our results indicated that the magnetic compass orientation of European robins could not be disrupted by any of the relatively strong narrow-band electromagnetic fields employed here, but that the weak broadband field very efficiently disrupted their orientation.
note: Classified behavioural_response: loss of Emlen-funnel orientation under a field treatment. Contrary and null results are in conditions: the spring 2012 ~48 nT narrow-band fields gave non-significant orientation (p = 0.138 and 0.179) while dummies oriented, so a weak narrow-band field also left birds unoriented in that season; the narrow-band field run alongside the broadband field in autumn 2013 was ~48 nT, not the ~400 nT of spring 2013, so the abstract's 'relatively strong' covers fields of both intensities. Design limits: birds pre-selected for orientation, no randomised condition sequence described, no direct statistical comparison of broadband with control, broadband intensity calculated from a measured spectrum. The Results give p = 0.63 and 0.57 where the Figure 6 caption gives 0.603 and 0.557.
